import DocCardGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-card-group'
import DocCard from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-card'
import Tabs from '~/components/webkit/Tabs.vue'

In this tutorial, you will serve a one-page site from an [Object Storage](/en/documentation/platform/object-storage/) bucket and keep a copy of it in the Azion [cache](/en/documentation/platform/applications/cache/). You will watch the cache answer the page, publish a second version of the page, and purge the old copy so that the new version reaches every reader.

Every resource the tutorial creates links to one created before it:

1. The bucket holds the page. Its **Workloads Access** is read only, so the Application reads it and does not change it.
2. The [Connector](/en/documentation/platform/connectors/), of the Object Storage type, points to the bucket.
3. The [Application](/en/documentation/platform/applications/) has a cache setting and a request rule. On every path, the rule sends the request to the Connector and applies the cache setting.
4. The [Workload](/en/documentation/platform/workloads/) holds the domain that receives requests, and its deployment sets the Application that answers them.

The resources are the same in Azion Console, the Azion CLI, and the API. Select the interface you use, and every stage shows its steps.

---

## 1. Create the page

Create a directory for the tutorial and go to it:

```bash
mkdir cached-site
cd cached-site
```

Write the first version of the page to an `index.html` file:

```bash
echo '<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Cached site</title></head><body><h1>Version 1</h1></body></html>' > index.html
```

The directory holds `index.html`, whose heading reads `Version 1`.

---

## 2. Create the bucket and upload the page

Choose a name for the bucket. A bucket name is unique across all Azion accounts and takes 6 to 63 characters: lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or a number. Wherever a step shows `<your-bucket-name>`, use your name.

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

To create the bucket:

1. Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Object Storage**.
2. Select **+ Bucket**.
3. In **Name**, enter the name of your bucket.
4. Keep **Read Only** in **Workloads Access**.
5. Select **Save**.

The bucket appears in the list of buckets.

To upload the page:

1. In the list of buckets, select the name of your bucket.
2. Drag `index.html` onto the area that reads **Drag files here to add them to your bucket**.

The bucket lists `index.html` with 131 Bytes.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

Store the name of your bucket in a shell variable:

```bash
BUCKET=<your-bucket-name>
```

Create the bucket with read-only access for Workloads:

```bash
azion create storage bucket --name $BUCKET --workloads-access read_only
```

```text
Bucket created successfully
```

Upload the page:

```bash
azion create storage object --bucket-name $BUCKET --object-key index.html --source index.html
```

```text
Object created successfully
```

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

Store your personal token and the name of your bucket in shell variables. Replace `<your-personal-token>` with your token:

```bash
export AZION_API_TOKEN="<your-personal-token>"
BUCKET=<your-bucket-name>
```

Create the bucket with read-only access for Workloads:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/storage/buckets \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"name\": \"$BUCKET\", \"workloads_access\": \"read_only\"}"
```

```json
{"state":"executed","data":{"name":"cached-site-api-ezxfkm","workloads_access":"read_only",...}}
```

Upload the page as the body of a `POST` request to its object key. `Content-Type` sets the type of the object:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/storage/buckets/$BUCKET/objects/index.html \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: text/html' \
  --data-binary @index.html
```

```json
{"state":"executed","data":{"object_key":"index.html"}}
```

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

The bucket holds the page.

---

## 3. Create the Connector

The Connector points to the bucket. Its prefix `/` reads the objects at the root of the bucket, so a request for `/index.html` reads the object `index.html`.

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

To create the Connector:

1. Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Connectors**.
2. Select **+ Connectors**.
3. In **Name**, enter `cached-site`.
4. In **Connector Type**, select **Object Storage**.
5. In **Bucket**, select your bucket.
6. Keep `/` in **Prefix**.
7. Select **Save**.

The Console shows the message **Connector successfully created**.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

Write the Connector to a `connector.json` file. The file reads the name of the bucket from `BUCKET`:

```bash
cat > connector.json <<EOF
{
  "name": "cached-site",
  "type": "storage",
  "attributes": { "bucket": "$BUCKET", "prefix": "/" }
}
EOF
```

Create the Connector. `--type storage` keeps the CLI from asking for the type:

```bash
azion create connector --type storage --file connector.json
```

```text
Created Connector with ID 235616
```

Store the ID that your command printed. Replace `235616` with your ID:

```bash
CONNECTOR_ID=235616
```

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

Create the Connector:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/connectors \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"name\": \"cached-site\", \"type\": \"storage\", \"attributes\": {\"bucket\": \"$BUCKET\", \"prefix\": \"/\"}}" \
| tee connector.json
```

```json
{"state":"pending","data":{"id":235617,...,"active":true,"type":"storage","attributes":{"bucket":"cached-site-api-ezxfkm","prefix":"/"},...}}
```

```bash
CONNECTOR_ID=$(jq .data.id connector.json)
```

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

The Connector reads the bucket. It answers requests only after an Application sends them to it.

---

## 4. Create the Application

The Application needs three parts: the Application itself, a cache setting, and a rule that applies both the Connector and the cache setting. The cache setting holds two times:

- **Azion's cache keeps a copy for 3600 seconds**, one hour. During that hour, the copy answers requests, and the bucket is not read again.
- **A browser keeps the page for 60 seconds.** The Application sends this time in the `cache-control` header of the response.

The cache setting also keeps **Stale cache** on, which serves an expired copy for a short time while the cache fetches the page again from the bucket. The cache works in every Application, with no module to turn on.

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

To create the Application:

1. Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Applications**.
2. Select **+ Application**.
3. In **Name**, enter `cached-site`.
4. Select **Create**.

The Console opens the new Application on its **Main Settings** tab.

To create the cache setting:

1. Select the **Cache Settings** tab.
2. Select **+ Cache**.
3. In **Name**, enter `cached-site`.
4. In **Browser Cache**, select **Override cache settings**, and enter `60` in **Max Age**.
5. In **Cache**, keep **Override cache behavior**, and enter `3600` in **Max Age**.
6. Keep **Stale cache** on.
7. Select **Save**.

The Console shows the message **Cache Settings successfully created**.

To apply the Connector and the cache setting on every request:

1. Select the **Rules Engine** tab.
2. Select **+ Rule**.
3. In **Name**, enter `Serve and cache the bucket`.
4. Keep **Request Phase** selected.
5. In **Criteria**, keep `${uri}` and **starts with**, and enter `/` as the argument.
6. In **Behaviors**, replace **Deliver** with **Set Connector**, and select `cached-site` in the field that it adds.
7. Select **+ Add Behavior**. In the new behavior, select **Set Cache Policy**, and select `cached-site` in the field that it adds.
8. Select **Save**.

The rule appears in the request phase of the **Rules Engine** tab.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

Create the Application:

```bash
azion create application --name cached-site --active true
```

```text
Created Application with ID 1794600035
```

Store the ID. Replace `1794600035` with your ID:

```bash
APPLICATION_ID=1794600035
```

Write the cache setting to a `cache.json` file:

```bash
cat > cache.json <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "cached-site",
  "browser_cache": { "behavior": "override", "max_age": 60 },
  "modules": {
    "cache": { "behavior": "override", "max_age": 3600, "stale_cache": { "enabled": true } }
  }
}
EOF
```

Create the cache setting in the Application:

```bash
azion create cache-setting --application-id $APPLICATION_ID --file cache.json
```

```text
Created Cache Settings configuration with ID 394590
```

Store the ID. Replace `394590` with your ID:

```bash
CACHE_SETTING_ID=394590
```

Write the rule to a `rule.json` file. On every path, it sets the Connector and the cache setting:

```bash
cat > rule.json <<EOF
{
  "name": "Serve and cache the bucket",
  "criteria": [[{ "variable": "\${uri}", "conditional": "if", "operator": "starts_with", "argument": "/" }]],
  "behaviors": [
    { "type": "set_connector", "attributes": { "value": $CONNECTOR_ID } },
    { "type": "set_cache_policy", "attributes": { "value": $CACHE_SETTING_ID } }
  ]
}
EOF
```

Create the rule in the request phase:

```bash
azion create rules-engine --application-id $APPLICATION_ID --phase request --file rule.json
```

```text
Created Rules Engine with ID 1547942
```

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

Create the Application:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/applications \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"name": "cached-site"}' \
| tee application.json
```

```json
{"state":"pending","data":{"id":1794600036,...,"modules":{"cache":{"enabled":true},...},"active":true,...}}
```

```bash
APPLICATION_ID=$(jq .data.id application.json)
```

Create the cache setting in the Application:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/applications/$APPLICATION_ID/cache_settings \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"name": "cached-site", "browser_cache": {"behavior": "override", "max_age": 60}, "modules": {"cache": {"behavior": "override", "max_age": 3600, "stale_cache": {"enabled": true}}}}' \
| tee cache.json
```

```json
{"state":"executed","data":{"id":394591,...,"browser_cache":{"behavior":"override","max_age":60},"modules":{"cache":{"behavior":"override","max_age":3600,"stale_cache":{"enabled":true},...},...},...}}
```

```bash
CACHE_SETTING_ID=$(jq .data.id cache.json)
```

Add the rule that sets the Connector and the cache setting on every path:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/applications/$APPLICATION_ID/request_rules \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"name\": \"Serve and cache the bucket\", \"criteria\": [[{\"variable\": \"\${uri}\", \"conditional\": \"if\", \"operator\": \"starts_with\", \"argument\": \"/\"}]], \"behaviors\": [{\"type\": \"set_connector\", \"attributes\": {\"value\": $CONNECTOR_ID}}, {\"type\": \"set_cache_policy\", \"attributes\": {\"value\": $CACHE_SETTING_ID}}]}"
```

```json
{"state":"pending","data":{"id":1547943,"name":"Serve and cache the bucket","active":true,...,"behaviors":[{"type":"set_connector","attributes":{"value":235617}},{"type":"set_cache_policy","attributes":{"value":394591}}],...}}
```

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

The Application reads every request from the bucket through the Connector, and keeps a copy of each response in the cache.

---

## 5. Create the Workload

The Workload holds the domain, and its deployment sets the Application that answers its requests.

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

To create the Workload and its deployment:

1. Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Workloads**.
2. Select **+ Workload**.
3. In **Name**, enter `cached-site`.
4. In **Deployment Settings**, select `cached-site` in **Application**.
5. Select **Save**.

The list of Workloads shows the domain in the **Workload Domain** column, in the format `xxxxxxxxxxx.map.azionedge.net`.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

Create the Workload:

```bash
azion create workload --name cached-site
```

```text
Created Workload with ID 1794600630
```

Store the ID. Replace `1794600630` with your ID:

```bash
WORKLOAD_ID=1794600630
```

Create the Workload's deployment, which sets the Application:

```bash
azion create workload-deployment --workload-id $WORKLOAD_ID --name cached-site --strategy-type default --application-id $APPLICATION_ID
```

```text
Created Workload Deployment with ID 361455
```

Read the domain of the Workload:

```bash
DOMAIN=$(azion describe workload --workload-id $WORKLOAD_ID --format json | jq -r .workload_domain)
echo $DOMAIN
```

```text
qo18fn5hs3c.map.azionedge.net
```

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

Create the Workload:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/workloads \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"name": "cached-site"}' \
| tee workload.json
```

```json
{"state":"pending","data":{"id":1794600631,...,"workload_domain":"b8dwzmvwqjg.map.azionedge.net",...}}
```

```bash
WORKLOAD_ID=$(jq .data.id workload.json)
DOMAIN=$(jq -r .data.workload_domain workload.json)
```

Create the Workload's deployment, which sets the Application:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/workloads/$WORKLOAD_ID/deployments \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"name\": \"cached-site\", \"strategy\": {\"type\": \"default\", \"attributes\": {\"application\": $APPLICATION_ID}}}"
```

```json
{"state":"pending","data":{"id":361456,"current":true,"active":true,"strategy":{"type":"default","attributes":{"application":1794600036,"firewall":null,"custom_page":null}},...}}
```

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

Your domain has the same format as the examples, with different letters.

## 6. Request the page from the cache

A new Workload can take about ten minutes to propagate across the Azion network. Until then, the domain answers `404` with an HTML error page, and it can alternate between `404` and the page for a few minutes.

If you used the Console, set `DOMAIN` to your domain first, with `DOMAIN=<your-domain>`. Request the page:

```bash
curl "https://$DOMAIN/index.html"
```

Repeat the request every minute until the page returns three times in a row:

```html
<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Cached site</title></head><body><h1>Version 1</h1></body></html>
```

To see whether the cache answered, send the request header `Pragma: azion-debug-cache`. With it, the response carries the `x-cache` headers of Azion's cache. Request the page and print its cache headers:

```bash
curl --silent --output /dev/null --dump-header - --header 'Pragma: azion-debug-cache' "https://$DOMAIN/index.html" | grep -i -E '^(x-cache|x-cache-valid|cache-control):'
```

```text
x-cache: MISS from 179.191.172.49 with HTTP/2.0
x-cache-valid: 3600
cache-control: max-age=60
```

Each response carries three headers:

- **`x-cache`** names the server that answered and what it did. `MISS` means that the server had no copy: it read the page from the bucket and kept a copy. `HIT` means that the server answered from its copy, without reading the bucket.
- **`x-cache-valid`** is the time, in seconds, that the server keeps its copy: the 3600 seconds of the cache setting.
- **`cache-control`** carries the 60 seconds that a browser keeps the page.

Each server keeps its own copy, and your requests can reach more than one server. A server answers `MISS` the first time it receives the page, and `HIT` after that. Request the page 20 times and count the answers:

```bash
for i in $(seq 20); do
  curl --silent --output /dev/null --dump-header - --header 'Pragma: azion-debug-cache' "https://$DOMAIN/index.html" | grep -i '^x-cache:' | cut -d ' ' -f 2
done | sort | uniq -c
```

```text
  20 HIT
```

Your count can include a few `MISS` answers, one for each server that received the page for the first time. The requests also leave a copy of `Version 1` on each server they reach. If the counts add up to less than 20, some requests got the `404` page because the Workload is still propagating: wait a minute and run the loop again.

The cache answers the page from its copies.

---

## 7. Publish a new version and purge the old copy

Write the second version of the page over `index.html`:

```bash
echo '<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Cached site</title></head><body><h1>Version 2</h1></body></html>' > index.html
```

Upload it to the same key. The upload replaces the object in the bucket:

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

1. Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Object Storage**.
2. In the list of buckets, select the name of your bucket.
3. Drag the new `index.html` onto the area that reads **Drag files here to add them to your bucket**.

The Console replaces the object without asking for confirmation, and the **Last Modified** column of `index.html` shows the time of the upload.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

Run the upload command again:

```bash
azion create storage object --bucket-name $BUCKET --object-key index.html --source index.html
```

```text
Object created successfully
```

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

Send the upload request again:

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/storage/buckets/$BUCKET/objects/index.html \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: text/html' \
  --data-binary @index.html
```

```json
{"state":"executed","data":{"object_key":"index.html"}}
```

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

Request the page 10 times and count the versions in the responses:

```bash
for i in $(seq 10); do
  curl --silent "https://$DOMAIN/index.html" | grep -o 'Version [0-9]'
done | sort | uniq -c
```

```text
  10 Version 1
```

The bucket holds `Version 2`, but a server that has a copy of `Version 1` keeps answering with it until the copy expires, up to one hour later. Only a server with no copy reads the bucket and answers `Version 2`, so your count can include a few. A count below 10 in total means that some requests got the `404` page; run the loop again. Until the copies expire, your readers can get either version.

Purge the old copy of the page from the cache. The purge takes the URL without `https://`:

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

1. Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Real-Time Purge**.
2. Select **+ Purge**.
3. In **Layer Settings**, keep **Cache** selected.
4. In **Purge Type**, select **URL**.
5. In **Arguments List**, enter your domain followed by `/index.html`, in the format `xxxxxxxxxxx.map.azionedge.net/index.html`.
6. Select **Save**.

The purge appears in the list of **Real-Time Purge**, with **Cache** in **Layer** and **Url** in **Type**.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

```bash
azion purge --urls "$DOMAIN/index.html"
```

```text
Purge carried out successfully
```

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

```bash
curl --silent https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/purge/url \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"items\": [\"$DOMAIN/index.html\"], \"layer\": \"cache\"}"
```

```json
{"state":"executed","data":{"items":["b8dwzmvwqjg.map.azionedge.net/index.html"],"layer":"cache"}}
```

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

A few seconds after the purge, count the versions again:

```bash
for i in $(seq 10); do
  curl --silent "https://$DOMAIN/index.html" | grep -o 'Version [0-9]'
done | sort | uniq -c
```

```text
  10 Version 2
```

Every response carries `Version 2`. The purge removed the copy of `Version 1` from every server, so the first request to each server reads the new page from the bucket, and the next ones answer from the new copy.

---

## 8. (Optional) Delete the resources

The site keeps running on your domain after the tutorial. If you want to remove the resources, delete them in this order: the Workload, the Application, the Connector, and the page. Deleting the Workload also deletes its deployment, and deleting the Application also deletes its cache setting and its rule. The Connector is deleted only after the Application, because the rule of the Application references it.

A bucket is deleted only when it is empty and no object was removed from it in the last 24 hours. To remove the bucket too, delete the page first, and the bucket one day later.

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

To delete the Workload:

1. Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Workloads**.
2. In the `cached-site` row, open the actions menu and select **Delete**.
3. In the **Delete Workload** dialog, enter `cached-site`.
4. Select **Delete**.

Repeat the steps in **Applications** for the `cached-site` Application, then in **Connectors** for the `cached-site` Connector. If the Application still exists, the Console refuses to delete the Connector with this message:

```text
Cannot delete an Connector referenced by another resource. References: EdgeApplicationRuleEngine - id: 1547941
```

To delete the page:

1. Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Object Storage**.
2. In the list of buckets, select the name of your bucket.
3. In the `index.html` row, open the actions menu and select **Delete**.
4. In the **Delete File** dialog, enter `index.html`.
5. Select **Delete**.

One day later, delete the bucket: in the list of buckets, open the actions menu of your bucket, select **Delete**, and enter the name of the bucket in the **Delete bucket** dialog. Before the 24 hours pass, the Console answers with this error:

```text
Unable to delete a non-empty bucket. Additionally, objects deleted within the last 24 hours are also taken into consideration.
```

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

Delete the Workload, the Application, and the Connector:

```bash
azion delete workload --workload-id $WORKLOAD_ID
```

```text
Workload 1794600630 was successfully deleted
```

```bash
azion delete application --application-id $APPLICATION_ID
```

```text
Application 1794600035 was successfully deleted
```

```bash
azion delete connector --connector-id $CONNECTOR_ID
```

```text
Connector 235616 was successfully deleted
```

Delete the page:

```bash
azion delete storage object --bucket-name $BUCKET --object-key index.html
```

```text
Object index.html was deleted successfully
```

Schedule the deletion of the bucket. `--yes` answers the prompt that the bucket is not empty:

```bash
azion delete storage bucket --name $BUCKET --yes
```

```text
Delete all objects from bucket
Deleting objects...
Bucket deletion was scheduled successfully
```

Right after the command, the bucket still appears in `azion list storage bucket`.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

Delete the Workload, the Application, the Connector, and the page:

```bash
for resource in workloads/$WORKLOAD_ID applications/$APPLICATION_ID connectors/$CONNECTOR_ID storage/buckets/$BUCKET/objects/index.html; do
  curl --silent --request DELETE https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/$resource \
    --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN"
  echo
done
```

```text
{"state":"pending"}
{"state":"pending"}
{"state":"pending"}
{"state":"pending"}
```

One day later, delete the bucket:

```bash
curl --silent --request DELETE https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/storage/buckets/$BUCKET \
  --header "Authorization: Token $AZION_API_TOKEN"
```

Before the 24 hours pass, the call answers `400` with the code `17006`:

```json
{"errors":[{"code":"17006","title":"Cannot Delete Non Empty Bucket","detail":"Unable to delete a non-empty bucket. Additionally, objects deleted within the last 24 hours are also taken into consideration.","status":"400","source":{"pointer":"/data"}}]}
```

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

The account no longer holds the Workload, the Application, the Connector, or the page. The removal of the Workload also propagates, so the domain can keep answering for a few minutes.
